package.name: aws-dynamodb
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# THE FIRST AWS PACKAGE AS MANIFESTS, and what proves `awsSigV4`.
#
# DynamoDB's HTTP API is one endpoint per region, an `X-Amz-Target` header naming the
# operation, and a JSON body. There is nothing else to it: take the signer and the
# translator out of @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb and that is what remains. The client, its
# cache and its four Command classes collapse into one call per node.
#
# TWO EXECUTOR CAPABILITIES CARRY IT, both using AWS's own libraries rather than anything
# written here:
#   awsSigV4              signs the request (@smithy/signature-v4)
#   encoding: dynamodbJson  translates values to and from DynamoDB's type tags
#                         (@aws-sdk/util-dynamodb, the same translator the DocumentClient
#                         uses). It cannot be an expression: the walk is recursive.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/aws-dynamodb/`.

name: aws-dynamodb
displayName: AWS DynamoDB
description: Read and write records in AWS DynamoDB
version: 2.0.0
category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751473913/gravity/icons/DynamoDB.png

features:
  - Put a record, read one by key
  - Query and scan on demand over a service edge
  - Signed with AWS Signature Version 4, no SDK in the node

# Regional endpoints, one subdomain level: dynamodb.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com.
allowedHosts:
  - "**.amazonaws.com"

requires:
  credential: [awsSigV4]
  transport: [json]
  executorVersion: ">=1.2.0"

credentials.awsCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# Transcribed from plugin-base's shared AWSCredential, NAME AND FIELDS UNCHANGED so
# credentials already stored against `awsCredential` keep resolving. Every AWS package
# shares this one, exactly as they shared the TypeScript definition.
#
# sessionToken is NEW, and additive. The retired definition had no such field, so anyone on
# temporary credentials (an assumed role, anything via STS) could not use these nodes at
# all. The signer sends and signs it only when it is filled in.

name: awsCredential
displayName: AWS Credentials
description: AWS credentials for AWS services (DynamoDB, S3, Bedrock, and the rest)
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html

properties:
  - name: accessKeyId
    displayName: Access Key ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Access Key ID
    placeholder: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
  - name: secretAccessKey
    displayName: Secret Access Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Secret Access Key
    placeholder: ""
  - name: region
    displayName: AWS Region
    type: string
    required: false
    default: us-east-1
    description: The region your tables live in
    placeholder: us-east-1
  - name: sessionToken
    displayName: Session Token
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: true
    description: Only for temporary credentials from STS or an assumed role. Leave empty for a long-lived key.
    placeholder: ""

shared.dynamodb.yaml:
# The one call shape every DynamoDB operation shares.
#
# There is no per-operation URL: everything goes to the regional endpoint and the
# `X-Amz-Target` header picks the operation. A node $refs this and adds that header plus a
# body, which is why these manifests read like RPC rather than REST.

call: &call
  method: POST
  url: "return 'https://dynamodb.' + credentials.awsCredential.region + '.amazonaws.com/'"

  credential:
    scheme: awsSigV4
    service: dynamodb

  headers:
    # AWS's own JSON dialect, NOT application/json. The wrong one is a 400 that complains
    # about the body rather than the header, which sends you looking in the wrong place.
    Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0

  transport: json
  # Plain JSON in the manifest; type tags on the wire. See api.schema.json#encoding.
  encoding: dynamodbJson

  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    # DynamoDB reports throttling as a 400 with a specific error type, not a 429. A blanket
    # 400 retry would resend genuinely malformed requests forever, so only the server-side
    # statuses are retried and a throughput problem surfaces instead of being hidden.
    on: [500, 502, 503, 504]

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# PutItem returns an EMPTY BODY on success, which is why `success` is not read off the
# reply: reaching here at all means the call did not throw, and a 400 (a failed condition,
# a bad table) already errors before any row fires.

- emit: success
  from: response
  value: "return true"

# The id the record carries, under whichever of the usual names it uses. Reported from what
# was SENT, since the reply says nothing.
- emit: itemId
  from: response
  value: >-
    return [(config.record || {}), (signal || {})]
      .map(r => r.id || r.Id || r.ID || r.universalId)
      .filter(Boolean)[0] || ''
files.api/run.yaml:
# One signed PutItem. The record is written as PLAIN JSON here; `encoding: dynamodbJson`
# on the shared call adds the type tags, so nothing in this file spells out {"S": ...}.

- $ref: dynamodb#call
  name: put
  headers:
    X-Amz-Target: DynamoDB_20120810.PutItem
    Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0

  body:
    TableName: "{{ config.tableName }}"
    # The signal is the fallback, so an upstream node can supply the record without the
    # panel repeating it. Config wins when it is set, which is what an explicit setting means.
    Item: "return (config.record && Object.keys(config.record).length) ? config.record : (signal || {})"
    ConditionExpression: "{{ config.conditionExpression }}"
    ExpressionAttributeNames: >-
      return Object.keys(config.expressionAttributeNames || {}).length
        ? config.expressionAttributeNames : undefined
    ExpressionAttributeValues: >-
      return Object.keys(config.expressionAttributeValues || {}).length
        ? config.expressionAttributeValues : undefined
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [tableName, record]
  properties:
    tableName:
      type: string
      title: Table Name
      description: The DynamoDB table to write to
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    record:
      type: object
      title: Record
      description: The record to write, as a plain object. Type tags are added for you.
      default: {}
      "ui:field": template
    conditionExpression:
      type: string
      title: Condition Expression
      description: >-
        Optional condition the write must satisfy, e.g. attribute_not_exists(universalId)
        to refuse an overwrite.
      default: ""
    expressionAttributeNames:
      type: object
      title: Expression Attribute Names
      description: Substitution tokens for attribute names used in the condition
      default: {}
      "ui:field": code
    expressionAttributeValues:
      type: object
      title: Expression Attribute Values
      description: Values used in the condition, as plain values
      default: {}
      "ui:field": code

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order":
  [authRequired, authRole, tableName, record, conditionExpression, expressionAttributeNames, expressionAttributeValues]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Record data, used when config.record is left empty
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: success
    type: boolean
    description: Whether the write was accepted
  - name: itemId
    type: string
    description: The record's own id, when it carries one

credentials:
  - name: awsCredential
    required: true
    displayName: AWS
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: DynamoDB
kind: PromiseNode

name: DynamoDB
category: Storage & Data
color: "#FF9900"

description: Write a record to an AWS DynamoDB table

whenToUse: >-
  Pick to put ONE record into a DynamoDB table as a step in a flow. Reading a record back,
  and exposing the full operation set to an attached agent, are different jobs with their
  own nodes.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NEVER cacheable: it writes. Reusing a prior output would skip the write entirely while
  # reporting that it happened.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# WRITES A REAL RECORD. Point tableName at a scratch table before running.

testData:
  config:
    tableName: Users
    record:
      universalId: user-1001
      name: Ada Lovelace
      email: ada@example.com
      createdAt: "2026-06-27T12:00:00Z"
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    success: "return output.success === true"
    itemId: "return output.itemId === 'user-1001'"
